$why: D84. `frontend/src/api/mock.ts` is LOOSER THAN CORED, and 61 test files build
their masters through it — plus the dev browser itself, because App.tsx's
dev-client switch hands the same mock to a real operator. Every one of those
tests is therefore measured against an engine that enforces less than the
server does, which is how three separate lanes shipped a green suite over a
This corpus is the ONE place that says what cored actually does. Two runners
read it: a vitest one over createMockClient() (`api/contract/`), and a script
one over live cored (`scripts/contract-mock-vs-cored.mts`). When they disagree,
the mock is wrong until this file says otherwise.
$shape: REFUSAL-SHAPED, NEVER VALUE-SHAPED. A row says which bodies are turned away
and with what sentence — not what a figure computes to. Value equality between
a mock and a server is a much bigger promise than this gate can keep, and a
gate that overpromises gets deleted by the first person it inconveniences.
⚠️ THE ONE VALUE DIVERGENCE THAT MATTERS CANNOT BE EXPRESSED HERE and is a
hand-written scenario in BOTH runners instead: an order book with NO as-on,
over a passed due date, gives mock `is_overdue:false` and cored `true`. It is
called out at the scenario, not hidden in a format that cannot hold it.
$provenance: EVERY `expect` BELOW WAS OBSERVED ON THE WIRE against a cored verified fresh
by symbol — not read off a handoff.
- an unknown group answers 404, not 422 (measured 2026-08-22; the recon
predicted 422). Still true.
⛔⛔ AND ONE OF THIS FILE'S OWN MEASUREMENTS WAS WRONG. It recorded, on
2026-08-22, that 'a DUPLICATE STOCK ITEM NAME IS ACCEPTED (201, a new id)',
contradicting the recon — and register row D90 was raised, and a USER
DECISION taken, on the strength of it. Re-measured the same day while
implementing that decision: cored REFUSES an exact duplicate with 422, and
`UNIQUE (company_id, name)` has been on `stock_item` since migration 0005.
The recon was right. This file was wrong.
⚠️ THE LESSON IS NOT 'MEASURE LESS'. Measuring is what found the real
defect underneath: uniqueness was BYTE-EXACT, so 'Acme Traders' and
'acme traders' were two masters, indistinguishable in every picker. That
is the consequence D90 described, reached by a mechanism nobody had
measured, and it applied to LEDGERS and UNITS too. Migration 0075
normalises all three. The lesson is that a measurement is evidence, not
proof — and a measurement that OVERTURNS a documented claim deserves the
same scepticism as the claim it overturns.
The `stock-item-duplicate-name` divergence this file used to declare has
been DELETED rather than edited: it certified behaviour that never
existed.

mock_gaps.current: the mock ACCEPTS a ledger under a group that does not exist
why: NOT a decision — a GAP, pinned so closing it has to be deliberate and so it
cannot be quietly forgotten. cored resolves the group and answers 404; the
mock cannot, because `createGroup` STORES NOTHING and the mock models no
chart of accounts at all. Refusing on 'this group was never created here'
would refuse essentially every ledger every one of the 61 test files makes,
because cored SEEDS 28 standard groups on company create (migration 0003)
and tests reasonably rely on 'Sundry Debtors' existing.
The cheap fix is to give the mock that seeded list. NOT taken here because
the list would be a silent copy of the SQL with nothing to detect drift:
the client has no `listGroups`, so neither runner can compare the mock's
list to cored's. Closing this row properly means adding that read method
first, and that is a bigger change than this row.
⛔ RUNNER A ASSERTS THE GAP IS STILL THERE. When someone closes it that
assertion fails and they delete this entry — the only way a known gap
leaves this file on purpose rather than by accident.

deliberate_divergence.what: allow_negative_stock ROUND-TRIPS through the mock and switches nothing
deliberate_divergence.where: frontend/src/api/mock.ts — no negative-stock enforcement exists at all; labelled by src/api/companyFeatures.test.ts
deliberate_divergence.why: ⛔ A GAP, NOT A PREFERENCE, and it is here rather than in mock_gaps only because the corpus format cannot hold it. Register rows D5+D43 gave company.allow_negative_stock its write side, and the mock mirrors ALL of that faithfully: it stores the flag, 404s an unknown company, leaves an omitted field alone, and answers from its store rather than echoing the request. What it cannot mirror is the only thing the flag DOES. cored has two negative-stock enforcers — ledger.checkNegativeStock inside the post tx, and the deferred check_stock_not_negative() constraint trigger — and the mock has NEITHER: its post never computes a closing position, so an outward move below zero is accepted whichever way the flag is set, and setting it false makes the mock refuse nothing. NOT EXPRESSIBLE AS A ROW, which is the whole reason it is filed here: this corpus is refusal-shaped ($shape) — a row names a body that is turned away and the sentence it is turned away with — while this is a VALUE that round-trips and an ABSENT REFUSAL, a shape with no body to send and no sentence to compare. A row asserting the mock refuses would fail forever; one asserting it accepts would certify the gap as correct. ⚠️ IT IS STILL ASSERTED STILL-OPEN, just not from here: the last case in src/api/companyFeatures.test.ts fails the day the mock grows an enforcer, and whoever closes it deletes that case and this entry together. The accept/refuse pair that is D5's real oracle is on the wire only — frontend/scripts/drive-l15-d5.mjs, read back out of Postgres.
